CHIEF COMPLAINT
Second opinion regarding hyperextension injury to right index finger sustained in motor vehicle accident.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Philip Gutierrez is a 50-year-old male presenting for a second opinion regarding a hyperextension injury to his right index finger sustained in a motor vehicle accident in March 2026. The patient was a passenger in a car that was rear-ended multiple times, which caused him to stretch out his right index finger. He reports the finger felt like it "went back" and has been painful since the accident, approximately three months ago. He notes persistent swelling, inability to make a fist, and pain that is sometimes unbearable, even with driving. He has been seeing an orthopedist and occupational therapist and underwent MRI imaging. He was initially offered an A1 pulley injection but declined due to concerns about steroid reactions. He reports conflicting information from his previous providers regarding whether injection would worsen the tear. He is right-handed and works as an x-ray technician, so functional use of this hand is important to him.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis. Reports itching reaction to methylprednisolone.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication (specific name not specified). History of methylprednisolone causing itching reaction.

ALLERGIES
Reaction to dexamethasone causing heart to race. Itching reaction to methylprednisolone.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: X-ray technician. Right-handed. Drove himself to the appointment.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient is a pleasant, cooperative, healthy-appearing male in no acute distress. Heart rate regular rate and rhythm with 2+ radial pulse. No swelling or bruising in the palm over the volar surface of the index finger. Normal creases slightly diminished over the PIP of the index finger compared to the middle finger. Index finger rests in a 10-degree PIP-flexed position. Tenderness on palpation at the MCP joint and along the flexor tendon sheath. Decreased sensation noted over the finger. Patient able to bend and straighten the finger with difficulty and pain. Able to make a fist. Full active range of motion examination performed. All extensors intact, collateral ligaments intact.

RESULTS
X-rays (four views of right hand): No bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits on the right hand, no soft tissue shadows of concern, no arthritis.

MRI from 4/24/2021: Focal soft tissue swelling over the right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of the right flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) tendon, fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) and FDS tendons. Radial and ulnar collateral ligaments of the index MCP joint intact, MCP joint capsule intact, extensor tendons intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-traumatic severe stenosing tenosynovitis of the right index finger with partial-thickness tear of the FDS tendon. Plan includes steroid injection with betamethasone (celestone) 1 cc plus lidocaine 0.5 cc to the flexor tendon sheath. Injection was attempted twice due to patient's significant pain response to needle introduction; small palmar vein was punctured during second attempt, controlled with bandage. Patient counseled on importance of therapeutic steroid and reassured regarding safety. Prescribed icing and ibuprofen this evening. Patient advised that injection will take 3-5 days to feel better with continued improvement over the next couple of weeks. Emphasized that patient has intact extensors and collateral ligaments, so no risk of tearing or breaking bone with movement. Recommended return to occupational therapy for active and passive range of motion exercises with goal of full ROM and no restrictions. Outpatient physical therapy prescription written for once weekly for six weeks. Patient counseled that he is safe to drive. Patient was told he may need repeat injections.
